   115	  - `mode`: `"units"`; `mps` and `mps_failed`: false;
   116	  - `outcome`: the first that applies of `"invalid_units"` (manifest unreadable, invalid or with fewer than four units), `"failed"` (an executed invocation exited nonzero), `"baseline_mismatch"`, `"outputs_mismatch"`, `"skipped"` (no `c2` or `c4` arm counted), otherwise `"measured"`;
   117	  - `units_total`: N, or null for `invalid_units`; `sample`: four rows `{index, cost_s}` in sample order, `index` being the manifest position, or `[]` for `invalid_units`. No unit identifier or output path appears in the file;
   118	  - `baseline_match` and `outputs_match`: booleans, or null when not evaluated;
   119	  - `serial_wall_s`: the mean wall of the counted `a` arms; `separate_wall_s`: the mean wall of the counted `b` arms; each a finite positive number or null;
   120	  - `batches`: exactly two rows, n=2 then n=4, each exactly `{n, wall_s, all_ok, skipped, factor}`: `wall_s` is the mean wall of the executed `c<n>` arms or null when none ran, `skipped` is true when none ran, `all_ok` is true when at least one ran and every executed one counted, and `factor` is `serial_wall_s / wall_s` when `all_ok` is true and `outcome` is `measured`, otherwise null;
   121	  - `arms`: exactly eight rows in the fixed order, each exactly `{label, wall_s, all_ok, skipped, cpu_s, effective_cores, busy_fraction, mem_available_min_kb, threads_max, invocations}`, with `label` from `a-1` to `a-2`; numbers are finite and nonnegative, or null when the arm did not run; `invocations` lists the executed invocations in launch order, each exactly `{units, rc, wall_s, cpu_s, max_rss_kb, nivcsw, inblock, oublock}`, `units` being sample positions;
   122	  - `nproc`: `os.cpu_count()`; `mem_total_kb`: `MemTotal` from `/proc/meminfo`;
   123	  - `factor`: the largest non-null batch factor, or null.
   124	  The factor compares the baseline's own serial mode with concurrent invocations over the same units, so per-invocation start-up costs count against it; `separate_wall_s` minus `serial_wall_s` shows that cost. The probe exits 0 whenever it writes the file and 2 when it cannot.
   125	- The pipeline validates a unit-mode file against the exact shape above, including each batch factor and `factor` as the largest batch factor, before copying it into the packet; anything else gives `concurrency: null`. Bounds and propose read only `factor`, `mps` and `mps_failed`, so they treat a unit-mode factor like a command-mode one, and a measured unit-mode factor below 1.05 is a valid negative finding (`mps` and `mps_failed` both false).
   126	
   127	## C/receipts/ and stage failure signatures
   128	- Every box command (uploads, probe, setup attempts, anchor execution, profiling, implementation) runs through `m5/boxrun.sh`; every receipt is `C/receipts/NNNN-<operation>.json`. Operations are `upload`, `probe`, `setup`, `anchors`, `profile`, `concurrency`, `implement-baseline`, `adapter-smoke`, `implement-state`, `implement-upload`, `implement-patch`, `setup-method`, `run-method`, `run-tests`; numbering continues across existing receipts. Receipt/log IDs contain no benchmark labels.
   129	- Receipts use the boxrun format: `{name, rc, timed_out, wall_s, budget_s, overrun, fetched, started_utc, ended_utc, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known}`. `name` is the receipt ID; `rc` is an integer remote exit code or null; `timed_out` and `fetched` are booleans; `wall_s` is nonnegative integer elapsed seconds; `budget_s` is the positive integer timeout supplied to boxrun; `overrun` is boolean, true on timeout or when measured wall_s exceeds budget_s; timestamps are UTC strings. Remote `out/` is fetched using the unchanged boxrun interface. After the remote command finishes, boxrun fetches remote `out/` and then the operation log; a fetch that fails is retried up to four more times, waiting 60 s before each retry (environment `BOXRUN_FETCH_WAIT_S` overrides the wait, for tests), and `fetched` is true only when both fetches succeed. A retry repeats only the fetch, never the remote command. Retry waits count in `wall_s`. Receipt contents stay in control; runtime logs stay in agent results.
   130	- Failed reproduce/profile signatures have fixed `error_class`: `infra` for unavailable box execution/receipts, failed upload, or failed fetch after a successful command, or a fixed profiler infrastructure marker; `install` for failed setup after the bounded repairs; `anchor` for an anchor-run failure or a failed anchor; `parse` for missing/invalid output files, unavailable harness files, or a nonzero profile command exit; `numeric` for a parsed profile that fails the stage-count, process-wrapper, coverage, or GPU telemetry gate. Exit codes are 4 for anchor failures, 3 for timeouts and 2 for the other failures. `infra` is added to the shared v1 error-class enum so the v2 envelope remains v1-valid. Box/fetch stdout and stderr are never copied into operator signatures.
   131	- Any box receipt with rc=124 or timed_out=true records a timeout, even when fetch fails. A final timeout fails its stage with `error_class: timeout`, exit 3. Authored setup and anchor scripts consume their existing repairs (at most four for setup, two for anchors), and method/test scripts their one bounded repair; method/test timeout repairs expose only the fixed timeout count plus budget/elapsed/overrun seconds, never test content. Transport, patch, probe, integrity and immutable evaluator commands permit one identical retry under the same budget (under keys `setup`, `anchors` and `profile`, the budget resolved at the retry's start, U47), without editing scientific payloads or trusted scorers. A second timeout stops that operation and stage. The fixed profiler permits no repair or execution retry; its first timeout stops profiling with `error_class: timeout`.
   132	- Reproduce, profile, implement and evaluate facts optionally add exactly typed timeout fields `{timed_out: boolean, budget_s: nonnegative integer, overrun: boolean}` when a box timeout occurs. `timed_out=true` records any attempt timing out, `budget_s` is the latest timed-out command's budget, and `overrun` is true when any timed-out receipt overruns. These fields survive a successful bounded repair; stage status then reflects the repaired result. Older records and SKIPPED/stub records retain their existing fact keys. No command output or new free-text fields enter signatures.
   133	- Numeric ratio facts accept finite JSON numbers, including integer spellings such as `0` and `1`; booleans remain invalid. This permits fully timed profiles to emit the capped fraction `1`.
   134	- Every stage records its own elapsed wall-clock seconds in v1 `wall_s`, excluding signature emission. SKIPPED stages measure only their skip handling, never the prior stage's duration.
   135	- Runner results add boolean `tokens_known`, true when the provider reports input/output usage (including reported zeros). wf exposes `agent.usage()` as a cumulative snapshot `{calls, tokens_in, tokens_out, unknown}`; `unknown` counts runner attempts without usage. Repairs, failed attempts, shadow calls, and fallbacks all contribute; cached calls do not incur usage. Compatible runners without `tokens_known` are accepted when their input/output counts are integers.

   179	    Run FroDock on a single receptor-ligand complex and generate `n_solutions` docking solutions.

   202	        n_solutions : int

   210	    complex_kind = str(complex_config["kind"])
   211	    complex_receptor = Path(complex_config["receptor"])
   212	    complex_ligand = Path(complex_config["ligand"])
   213	    results_dir = Path(params["results_dir"])
   214	    n_solutions = int(params["n_solutions"])
   215	    mpi_np = int(params.get("mpi_np", 8))
   216	    force = bool(params["force"])
   217	
   218	    results_path_complete = results_dir / f"frodock/{complex_id}/{complex_kind}_decoys/"
   219	    if not force and (results_path_complete / "model_1.pdb").exists():
   220	        log.info(
   221	            f"Skipping {complex_id} {complex_kind} because it already exists in {results_path_complete}"
   222	        )
   223	        return

   225	    frodock(

   230	        complex_kind,

     1	Can increased parallelism in protein–protein docking improve the recovery of experimentally observed binding poses, particularly for AAV capsid–receptor interactions?
